title: Link Between Size of Endowment Funds and Differences in Student Educational Resources, Expenditure and Opportunities
what_it_is: Link Between Size of Endowment Funds and Differences in Student Educational Resources, Expenditure and Opportunities

sections.label: Government matching grants tertiary education
sections.summary: Since 1991 the Government gave 1:1 matching grants for tertiary donations, raised to 1.5:1 in 2010 for AUs and 3:1 for newer institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Since 1991, the Government has encouraged donations to tertiary education by providing 1:1 matching grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: This was raised to 1.5:1 in 2010 for AUs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: For the newer institutions, for example, the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) and Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS), the Government further enhanced our support to them by granting them sizeable seed monies to start up their endowment fund, as well as more generous matching grants at 3:1.

sections.label: Singaporean student subsidy
sections.summary: Singaporean students receive a subsidy of around 75% of costs regardless of which AU they are enrolled in.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Regardless of which AU they are enrolled in, Singaporean students receive a subsidy of around 75% of costs.

sections.label: Endowment funds and monitoring
sections.summary: NUS has about $4 billion and SUSS about $400 million in endowments, which may support scholarships, professorships, teaching and research.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The National University of Singapore, I understand, has an endowment of about $4 billion and the Singapore University of Social Sciences of about $400 million.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And these endowment funds may be used by the universities to support scholarships, professorships, teaching and research.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, while I do not begrudge the more established universities for their success at fundraising and using funds, I do wonder if the Ministry could monitor the use of endowment funds to contribute to teaching and research, and if it results in disproportionate access or quality, if the Ministry could use that as a consideration when granting operating funds to the universities.

sections.label: NUS existence duration
sections.summary: The National University of Singapore has been in existence for 114 years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The National University of Singapore (NUS) has been in existence for 114 years.
